title: The Altar of Hands
text: A stone table in the dark, set with hands the way another table would be set with plates. Some are wax, some are bone, and one is still warm. In the middle of the stone is a hollow worn smooth, shaped for exactly one more, and it calls to you.

options.label: Place the frailest hand inside the hollow, giving in to the allure of the ancient altar.

outcomes.text: The stone closes over the wrist and lets go. The hand that comes back is not quite theirs, and it is better.
The stone closes over the wrist, gentle as a mouth, and keeps what it took, gnawing at flesh freely offered.
A vision of the hand severed cleanly at the wrist falls over them after a few moments, and they recoil in horror.

options.label: Ignore the call of the altar. No good can come of this.

outcomes.text: Those who move on find their palms itch for days afterwards, yearning for what could have been.
